local_facts.claim: Orange County Superior Court states that the Harbor Justice Center – Newport Beach handles traffic, minor offenses, and criminal matters. Its criminal and traffic mailing address is 4601 Jamboree Road, Newport Beach, CA 92660-2595.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A Newport Beach criminal matter should be organized around the court date and department shown in the person’s own paperwork, with the Harbor Justice Center’s local criminal process in mind. The citation, release papers, and any later notice should be retained so an appearance is not missed and the setting can be confirmed.
local_facts.title: Newport Beach has a local criminal court venue

local_facts.claim: California Harbors and Navigation Code section 655 prohibits operating a vessel while under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or their combined influence, and separately prohibits operating a recreational vessel with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or more.
local_facts.why_it_matters: An alleged impaired operation on Newport Harbor is a vessel-law matter. The response may need to examine who was operating, the vessel’s location and course, the Harbor Patrol contact, testing timing and method, passengers, and the records maintained by the responding agency.
local_facts.title: Newport Harbor allegations can involve vessel DUI law

local_facts.claim: The City of Newport Beach says that the Orange County Sheriff’s Department Harbor Patrol-Marine Operations Bureau manages the emergency and law-enforcement services of Newport Harbor.
local_facts.why_it_matters: For a boating-under-the-influence allegation, the responding agency, written report, dispatch or radio records, and exact place of the contact may be important evidence. That differs from the record trail in an ordinary roadway stop.
local_facts.title: Harbor Patrol records can be central evidence

anchors.label: Base fine, first DUI conviction
anchors.detail: Vehicle Code section 23536(a) pairs this fine with 96 hours to six months in county jail on a first conviction under section 23152. Every penalty assessment in the case is calculated from this figure, not added to a flat total.

anchors.label: Orange County penalty assessment
anchors.detail: Government Code section 76000(a)(1) sets a countywide penalty of $7 for every $10 of fine, then lists a reduced figure for most counties. The entry for Orange County is $5.29.

anchors.label: Bail, first misdemeanor DUI
anchors.detail: The Orange County Superior Court 2026 Uniform Bail Schedule lists this amount for a first misdemeanor under Vehicle Code 23152(a) or (b), and states that bail on it is not doubled under Vehicle Code section 42009.
anchors.source_name: Orange County Superior Court 2026 Uniform Bail Schedule

anchors.label: Emergency response expense billed to the driver
anchors.detail: Government Code section 53155 caps at this amount what a public agency may recover for one incident from a driver whose intoxication caused an emergency response, separate from any fine.

fee_rows.stage: A defense fee tied to the outcome
fee_rows.note: Rule 1.5(c)(2) bars any agreement for, charge of, or collection of a contingent fee for representing a defendant in a criminal case.

fee_rows.stage: Written fee contract with the lawyer
fee_rows.note: Section 6148 requires a signed written contract, with a duplicate copy handed to the client, whenever total expense including fees is reasonably foreseeable above that line.

fee_rows.stage: State penalty assessment on the fine
fee_rows.note: Levied on every fine, penalty or forfeiture a court collects for a criminal offense, so it matches the base fine dollar for dollar.
Section 1465.7 levies it on the same base fine used for the section 1464 penalty, and forbids folding the surcharge back into that base.

fee_rows.stage: County alcohol and drug problem assessment
fee_rows.note: Levied on fines collected for a Vehicle Code 23152 or 23153 violation in a judicial district that takes part in the county assessment program.

fee_rows.share: $55 DUI reissue, $125 after an administrative per se action
fee_rows.note: The department fee schedule lists both figures, plus $100 for a zero tolerance suspension under 21 and a $15 administrative service fee.
